# Getting Started



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, jsonlite,
               tidygraph, ggraph)
```
:::



# Importing Kownledge Graph Data



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
kg <- fromJSON("data/MC1_graph.json")
```
:::



## Inspect structure



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
str(kg, max.level = 1)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 $ multigraph: logi TRUE
 $ graph     :List of 2

```


:::
:::



# Extracting the edges and nodes tables



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
nodes_tbl <- as_tibble(kg$nodes)
edges_tbl <- as_tibble(kg$links) 
```
:::

# Creating Knowledge Graph

## Mapping from node id to row index



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
id_map <- tibble(id = nodes_tbl$id,
                 index = seq_len(
                   nrow(nodes_tbl)))
```
:::



## Map source and target IDs to row indices



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
edges_tbl <- edges_tbl %>%
  left_join(id_map, by = c("source" = "id")) %>%
  rename(from = index) %>%
  left_join(id_map, by = c("target" = "id")) %>%
  rename(to = index)
```
:::



## Filter out any unmatched (invalid) edges



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
edges_tbl <- edges_tbl %>%
  filter(!is.na(from), !is.na(to))
```
:::



## Creating tidygraph



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
graph <- tbl_graph(nodes = nodes_tbl, 
                   edges = edges_tbl, 
                   directed = kg$directed)
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
class(graph)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

```

:::


## Visualising the sub-graph

### Filtering edges to only “MemberOf”



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
graph_memberof <- graph %>%
  activate(edges) %>%
  filter(`Edge Type` == "MemberOf")
```
:::



### Extracting only connected nodes (i.e., used in these edges)



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
used_node_indices <- graph_memberof %>%
  activate(edges) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(from, to) %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique()
```
:::



### Keeping only those nodes



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
graph_memberof <- graph_memberof %>%
  activate(nodes) %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number()) %>%
  filter(row_id %in% used_node_indices) %>%
  select(-row_id)  # optional cleanup
```
:::



### Plotting the sub-graph



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggraph(graph_memberof, 
       layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.5, 
                 colour = "gray") +
  geom_node_point(aes(color = `Node Type`), 
                  size = 1) +

                 repel = TRUE, 
                 size = 2.5) +
```

Based on the analysis of the knowledge graph data, Sailor Shift (node ID: 17255) does not have any direct "collaborated With" or "influenced By" relationships with other nodes. However, she maintains significant musical connections via edge types such as "Lyricist Of", "Lyrical Reference To", "Interpolates From", and "In Style Of". These suggest that her influence may be stylistic or lyrical, rather than formal collaborations or direct inspiration as per the dataset's encoded relationships. Hence, Sailor Shift’s role appears more implicit or thematic rather than through conventional influence or joint work.

## Step 3: Visualize the spread of Oceanus Folk over time

We plot a timeline of influenced nodes, grouped by year or genre:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Clean date (some may be NA or characters)
influenced_by_oceanus %>%
  filter(!is.na(release_date)) %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(release_date)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(influence_count = n()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = influence_count)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Spread of Oceanus Folk Influence Over Time",
       x = "Year", y = "Number of Influenced Songs/Artists")
```

By tracing outgoing edges such as "influencedBy", "InStyleOf", and "InterpolatesFrom" from Oceanus Folk nodes, we find a diverse group of artists and songs that have incorporated its themes and styles. The time-series visualization shows a gradual and sustained spread — with notable growth starting around 1990, suggesting rising popularity and cultural reach.
